loop.top3_why: The median combination (pool_full) shows the most stable per‑window performance (0.5947, 0.5345, 0.6815) and the lowest overall validation score (0.6038). It is robust to outlying models and, given the unstable ranking and correlated errors, a robust estimator is preferable. The trimmed‑mean and mean strategies, while slightly better on average, have higher variance across windows and are more sensitive to the unstable ranking. Thus the median strategy is expected to generalize best to the blind test window.
loop.top3_why_not: A (trimmed_mean) and C (mean) both have higher per‑window variance and rely on a fixed pool of nine models; with only three validation windows the weight estimation is noisy and the unstable ranking suggests that a robust estimator like the median will perform better. The small gaps in validation score are within noise, so the stability advantage of B outweighs the marginal score difference.
